## Boundaries

- Knowledge/methods belong in the wiki; use original cases to understand their application.
- Authored narration and recorded interaction are different evidence. Unknown motives/outcomes stay unknown.
- Observations describe sources. Adaptations below are proposals, not facts about what the trainer always does.
- Select for the current learner situation; do not force platform marketing or catchphrases into every reply.

## 1. Source observation

The headline states the role and experience of the person, followed by a phrase 'Turning “Just send me some options...” into Closed deals.'

**Dimension:** expression · **Scope:** linkedin · **Review:** unreviewed
**Situation:** Authored text on LinkedIn highlighting years of experience and subject-matter expertise.
**Qualification:** The expression is only observed on the LinkedIn profile, not across multiple channels.

- “Dubai Real Estate Sales Mentor &amp; Business Consultant | 11+ years Selling | 6+ years Coaching. Turning “Just send me some options…” into Closed deals.” — [ex-8483fbfa17002987](../wiki/sources/linkedin-olgasi-yaml-ef8e458ca5.md) (`linkedin-olgasi-yaml-ef8e458ca5:u000001`)

### Proposed adaptation — not observed behavior

**When:** Professional profiles or networks looking to highlight personal achievements and expertise
**Consider:** Structuring headlines with role, experience, and a capability slogan
**Limits:** Effectiveness in attracting engagement is unevaluated

## 2. Source observation

The speaker uses a dismissive tone to describe perceptions of Dubai being overhyped, emphasizing the focus on the exit rather than the city itself.

**Dimension:** expression · **Scope:** youtube · **Review:** unreviewed
**Situation:** A video discussing the Dubai real estate market, focusing on market strategies and perceptions.
**Qualification:** The observation is based on a single video transcript and may not represent a consistent pattern across multiple videos or other contexts.

- “Is Dubai over hype? No, but the thing where got hype is not most of you think it was. It was never the city, it was the exit.” — [ex-2435379ea871e866](../wiki/sources/youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2.md) (`youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2:u000027`)

### Proposed adaptation — not observed behavior

**When:** Discussing market perceptions in other real estate contexts.
**Consider:** Use a similar dismissive tone to challenge mainstream perceptions and refocus discussions on specific strategies or elements.
**Limits:** Not applicable to contexts requiring neutral or positive encouragement without critique.

## 3. Source observation

The speaker contrasts perceptions of Dubai as a bubble with an analogy about a social event to illustrate the market's returning to normality, saying 'everyone is dancing and they assume this is how the room looks like all the time. But this market isn't falling apart. It's just Tuesday.'

**Dimension:** expression · **Scope:** youtube · **Review:** unreviewed
**Situation:** Discussion on Dubai real estate market by a YouTube speaker, contrasting current perceptions of market normality with a past inflated perception depicted as a party.
**Qualification:** Observation based on a single YouTube example, identity of speaker not independently authenticated.

- “everyone is dancing and they assume this is how the room looks like all the time. But this market isn't falling apart. It's just Tuesday,” — [ex-2cb6702ae9616f3e](../wiki/sources/youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2.md) (`youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2:u000014`)

### Proposed adaptation — not observed behavior

**When:** Delivering a critical comparison of market conditions with exaggerated perceptions
**Consider:** Use an analogy of a social event or regular occurrence to depict the hyperbolic nature of market speculation.
**Limits:** Do not extend to markets without cultural familiarity with the analogy or in written analyses favoring data over metaphor.

## 6. Source observation

The post uses sarcasm and humor to critique conventional sales advice by labeling them as 'Bad advice.'

**Dimension:** expression · **Scope:** linkedin · **Review:** unreviewed
**Situation:** LinkedIn post critiquing common sales errors through humor and sarcasm.
**Qualification:** Inherent to this particular authored example, without other platforms to support broader use.

- “Please follow carefully. 😇 Bad advice #1: Before you WhatsApp the lead, send an email first. Especially if they are European or American.” — [ex-fb65cff12bfca6e7](../wiki/sources/linkedin-posts-2026-09-25-how-to-spot-a-not-md-9cfd139d2f.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-09-25-how-to-spot-a-not-md-9cfd139d2f:u000001`)

### Proposed adaptation — not observed behavior

**When:** Critiquing overly adhered sales scripts or advice in written communication.
**Consider:** Employ sarcasm and humor by calling ineffective advice 'bad advice' to highlight its impracticality.
**Limits:** Avoid in contexts where sarcasm may be misunderstood or perceived as unprofessional, such as formal reports or highly cultural sensitive environments.

## 9. Source observation

The speaker compares Dubai's Expo 2020 experience to Riyadh's post-Expo 2030 win, highlighting market impacts and development timelines, while noting he's not predicting Riyadh will repeat Dubai's numbers.

**Dimension:** expression · **Scope:** youtube · **Review:** unreviewed
**Situation:** The speaker compares Dubai's experience after winning Expo 2020 to Riyadh's current situation post Expo 2030 win, focusing on potential market impacts and timelines for infrastructure development.
**Qualification:** The expression is a comparison within a particular context and does not claim or predict exact outcomes across different situations.

- “Dubai won Expo 2020 bid in November 2013, seven years before the event. And the market didn't wait for their Expo to open.” — [ex-b7079c04d062857f](../wiki/sources/youtube-video-2026-08-20-dubai-vs-saudi-real-estate-foreign-ownership-expo-2030-the-n-48ff0090d5.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-20-dubai-vs-saudi-real-estate-foreign-ownership-expo-2030-the-n-48ff0090d5:u000010`)
- “Riyadh won Expo twenty thirteen October twenty twenty three.” — [ex-b7079c04d062857f](../wiki/sources/youtube-video-2026-08-20-dubai-vs-saudi-real-estate-foreign-ownership-expo-2030-the-n-48ff0090d5.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-20-dubai-vs-saudi-real-estate-foreign-ownership-expo-2030-the-n-48ff0090d5:u000011`)
- “I'm not telling Riyadh will repeat Dubai numbers. It may not.” — [ex-b7079c04d062857f](../wiki/sources/youtube-video-2026-08-20-dubai-vs-saudi-real-estate-foreign-ownership-expo-2030-the-n-48ff0090d5.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-20-dubai-vs-saudi-real-estate-foreign-ownership-expo-2030-the-n-48ff0090d5:u000012`)

### Proposed adaptation — not observed behavior

**When:** When comparing historical economic impacts of major international events on cities to current scenarios.
**Consider:** Use historical precedents to frame expectations for similar current events, clarifying parallels without predicting direct repetition of outcomes.
**Limits:** Avoid implying direct causality or guaranteed outcomes, focus on illustrating similarities in scenarios.

## 10. Source observation

The speaker articulates their inability to predict the real estate market's future by emphasizing observation limits and the subjective nature of their opinion, shared across similar commentators.

**Dimension:** expression · **Scope:** youtube · **Review:** unreviewed

- “I can read regulations, I can see the transactions... but I cannot predict the future. ### Proposed adaptation — not observed behavior

**When:** When discussing market forecasts and acknowledging limitations in prediction.
**Consider:** Emphasize personal observations and limitations in predictive accounts, highlighting the uncertain nature of forecasting in volatile markets.
**Limits:** Avoid presenting subjective observations as comprehensive forecasts, maintain transparency about informational boundaries.

## 11. Source observation

The speaker uses a small percentage analogy \(two percent\) to highlight investors likely to act in early markets with incomplete data.

**Dimension:** expression · **Scope:** youtube · **Review:** unreviewed
**Situation:** The speaker uses a percentage analogy to discuss the early adoption risk in emerging markets, drawing on historical patterns observed in Dubai.
**Qualification:** This is an illustrative analogy specific to the context of the speaker's discussion and not a universal predictor of market behavior.

- “only probably a very small percentage, maybe even two percent of people going to move before it's going to be obvious for everyone else.” — [ex-7edbd9d938b2d0cf](../wiki/sources/youtube-video-2026-08-20-dubai-vs-saudi-real-estate-foreign-ownership-expo-2030-the-n-48ff0090d5.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-20-dubai-vs-saudi-real-estate-foreign-ownership-expo-2030-the-n-48ff0090d5:u000029`)

### Proposed adaptation — not observed behavior

**When:** When highlighting the behavior of early adopters within emerging investment markets.
**Consider:** Use analogy of small percentages to communicate the rarity and risk tolerance required for early investment action, reinforcing understanding of minority investor dynamics.
**Limits:** Do not generalize specific percentages across all markets and historical periods; maintain focus on illustrative purposes.

<a id="record-795211c717f491dd"></a>
## Confidence Building Exercise

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-05-26 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- A camera confidence exercise can help improve sales performance by overcoming self-monitoring behaviors.
  - “I'm going to give you two exercises. It's only five minutes a day and it's totally free.” — [lines 236-236](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000048`)
  - “So exercise number one, I call it the camera confidence test. It literally takes two minutes.” — [lines 240-240](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000049`)

### Goal

- To build confidence in sales conversations.
  - “Confidence is strained like a muscle.” — [lines 236-236](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000048`)

### Prerequisites

- Have a back camera to record yourself.
  - “You have to film yourself on the back camera, not the front one.” — [lines 240-240](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000049`)

### Steps

1. Film yourself on the back camera for approximately one minute.
  - “So, you film it, then you watch the video right away.” — [lines 240-240](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000049`)

2. Review the video and let your brain process the self-feedback.
  - “You don't have to do anything. Your brain will do the work.” — [lines 244-244](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000050`)

### Constraints

- The front camera should not be used as it divides attention.
  - “Because the front camera splits your brain in half.” — [lines 248-248](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000051`)

### Exceptions

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Original context

**olgasi** · lines 236-236 · spoken_turn

> You cannot script yourself out there. You can only outgrow it. And confidence is not delivered by watching more videos like this. Confidence is strained like a muscle. That's why I'm going to give you two exercises. It's only five minutes a day and it's totally free.

**olgasi** · lines 240-240 · spoken_turn

> you can start tonight. So exercise number one, I call it the camera confidence test. It literally takes two minutes. You have to film yourself on the back camera, not the front one. So put your phone approximately three meters away and time yourself in your head. It should be one minute, might not be exact one minute from the beginning, but then you're going to get better in it.

**olgasi** · lines 244-244 · spoken_turn

> So, you film it, then you watch the video right away. You don't have to do anything. Your brain will do the work. So, if you're doing this in the morning, talk about your plans for the day. And if you're filming in the evening, talk about how the day went. And that's it. By the way, why the back camera and not the front? Because the front camera splits your brain in half. One half is watching

**olgasi** · lines 248-248 · spoken_turn

> how do I look and the other half is trying to find the next word. That crashes you. That sounds like nonsense. This split is exactly the same split that's happening in your head on the real sales call. When you are nervous, half of your brain is monitoring how the client perceives you and the other half is trying to remember what to say. Neither half is actually with the client. The back camera kills the monitoring half. It teaches your brain to occupy the space.

## Strategy for reluctant real estate clients

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-04-29 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Create logical sequences to convince clients that waiting and seeing will cost them more.
  - “create a logical uh sequence that anyone whom I will be delivering to will be able to understand” — [lines 35-35](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-29-dubai-agents-if-client-say-i-ll-wait-answer-this-before-you-jdVOWThjPM0.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-29-dubai-agents-if-client-say-i-ll-wait-answer-this-before-you-4c0ad26e8a:u000002`)
  - “make those who are telling you wait and see to realize that waiting and seeing gonna cost them more” — [lines 87-87](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-29-dubai-agents-if-client-say-i-ll-wait-answer-this-before-you-jdVOWThjPM0.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-29-dubai-agents-if-client-say-i-ll-wait-answer-this-before-you-4c0ad26e8a:u000015`)

### Goal

- To persuade clients who say "I'll wait" to act now.
  - “make those who are telling you wait and see to realize that waiting and seeing gonna cost them more” — [lines 87-87](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-29-dubai-agents-if-client-say-i-ll-wait-answer-this-before-you-jdVOWThjPM0.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-29-dubai-agents-if-client-say-i-ll-wait-answer-this-before-you-4c0ad26e8a:u000015`)

### Prerequisites

- Clients should have common sense and not be naturally anxious.
  - “potentially if he has a common sense if this person is not naturally anxious” — [lines 35-35](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-29-dubai-agents-if-client-say-i-ll-wait-answer-this-before-you-jdVOWThjPM0.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-29-dubai-agents-if-client-say-i-ll-wait-answer-this-before-you-4c0ad26e8a:u000002`)

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Constraints

- This method may not work for clients who are anxious or would not buy due to other reasons even without current crises.

Those one like, I'm so sorry, I cannot help you with that.” — [lines 91-91](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-29-dubai-agents-if-client-say-i-ll-wait-answer-this-before-you-jdVOWThjPM0.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-29-dubai-agents-if-client-say-i-ll-wait-answer-this-before-you-4c0ad26e8a:u000016`)

- Some clients may be indecisive in general and unable to make buying decisions, not just real estate.

## Cold calling technique

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-07-16 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Cold calling is a fast way to generate opportunities if done correctly, avoiding common scripting that can lead to penalties.
  - “Coal calls when you ask, are you selling a rent in your property? Do not work. Please do not do this.” — [lines 148-148](../../data/youtube/video/2026-07-16-the-best-lead-generation-strategy-for-dubai-real-estate-agen-x9mWjb117AA.md) (`youtube-video-2026-07-16-the-best-lead-generation-strategy-for-dubai-real-estate-agen-92502d4649:u000029`)

### Goal

- Create opportunities quickly through effective cold calling.
  - “It's still the fastest way to create an opportunities in this market, but only if you know how to do that properly.” — [lines 136-136](../../data/youtube/video/2026-07-16-the-best-lead-generation-strategy-for-dubai-real-estate-agen-x9mWjb117AA.md) (`youtube-video-2026-07-16-the-best-lead-generation-strategy-for-dubai-real-estate-agen-92502d4649:u000026`)

### Prerequisites

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Steps

1. Develop specific techniques to find buyers and listings through cold calling.
  - “I created a specific technique which good for finding buyers and listings.” — [lines 140-140](../../data/youtube/video/2026-07-16-the-best-lead-generation-strategy-for-dubai-real-estate-agen-x9mWjb117AA.md) (`youtube-video-2026-07-16-the-best-lead-generation-strategy-for-dubai-real-estate-agen-92502d4649:u000027`)

## Sales Communication

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-04-08 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Sales communication is not just passing information from point A to point B. It's about communicating in a way that creates a desirable outcome for both you and the client by helping them discover on their own why an action is necessary.
  - “The communication skills is not your ability to pass the information from point A to point B. uh it's an ability for you to communicate in a way that creates the outcome which is desirable for you and desirable for the client.” — [lines 443-443](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-08-full-sales-course-dubai-real-estate-2026-off-plan-secondary-_0b6EYyDuPQ.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-08-full-sales-course-dubai-real-estate-2026-off-plan-secondary-e5e68c2962:u000097`)

### Goal

- To help clients discover on their own why an action is necessary and beneficial.
  - “is your ability to reflect on yourself while you're in communication and help the other person through your questions discover on his own why he needs this, why he needs this urgently” — [lines 455-455](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-08-full-sales-course-dubai-real-estate-2026-off-plan-secondary-_0b6EYyDuPQ.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-08-full-sales-course-dubai-real-estate-2026-off-plan-secondary-e5e68c2962:u000100`)

### Prerequisites

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Steps

1. Ask the client questions that help them discover for themselves why they need to act.
  - “Let me explain you. uh I recently got uh coaching client approaching me and we went into the coaching relationship” — [lines 443-443](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-08-full-sales-course-dubai-real-estate-2026-off-plan-secondary-_0b6EYyDuPQ.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-08-full-sales-course-dubai-real-estate-2026-off-plan-secondary-e5e68c2962:u000097`)

2. Reflect on your own communication style to ensure it helps clients discover their needs on their own.
  - “is your ability to reflect on yourself while you're in communication and help the other person through your questions discover on his own why he needs this” — [lines 455-455](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-08-full-sales-course-dubai-real-estate-2026-off-plan-secondary-_0b6EYyDuPQ.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-08-full-sales-course-dubai-real-estate-2026-off-plan-secondary-e5e68c2962:u000100`)

3. Convert statements into questions to prompt self-realization in clients.
  - “You understand? Instead of you convert your statements into questions. But it's not like you you put a question mark after statement.” — [lines 471-471](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-08-full-sales-course-dubai-real-estate-2026-off-plan-secondary-_0b6EYyDuPQ.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-08-full-sales-course-dubai-real-estate-2026-off-plan-secondary-e5e68c2962:u000104`)

### Constraints

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

2. On the first call, avoid making assumptions about the client's intentions.

<a id="record-97c2af6fdcc0b604"></a>
## Improved Conversion Strategy

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** advice · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-06-15T03:51:15.321000Z · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** post

### Summary

- If your conversion rate from lead to meeting is under five percent, examine the sales process before blaming the leads.
  - “If your conversion from lead to meeting is under five percent, look at the process before you blame the leads.” — [lines 10-38 part 4](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-06-15-1---that-was-the.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-06-15-1-that-was-the-md-88aee1b67b:u000004`)

### Original context

**authored text by olgasi** · lines 10-38 · authored_text

> call from a stranger.
> 
> These are people making a six, seven, sometimes eight-figure decision in a market they may barely understand yet. 
> And the first thing they get is a PDF on WhatsApp.
> 99% of those conversations end there. The client goes quiet. The agent blames the lead.
> What actually works looks nothing like that. 
> 
> Multiple touchpoints. Video calls. Materials that help the client understand why Dubai, why now, why with you. You are not selling a unit. You are building enough trust for someone to wire a significant amount of money across a border.
> When the process is built around that reality, conversion from social media lead to qualified prospect reaches thirty-five percent or more.
> The project becomes almost irrelevant. Because by then the client is engaging with you, not with a brochure.
> If your conversion from lead to meeting is under five percent, look at the process before you blame the leads.
> 
> Full break down of the pricess in the Off-plan course inside my academy.

**Publication:** 2026-06-15T03:51:15.321000Z · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** post

### Summary

- A traditional sales process involves calling the client, identifying their needs, sending brochures, and following up, but may only achieve a 1% conversion rate from social media leads to a qualified meeting.

**authored text by olgasi** · lines 10-38 · authored_text

> 1% - That was the conversion rate from social media leads to a qualified meeting.
> Nobody in the room thought the process was the problem.
> I first heard this sales process in 2015 when I entered this market. Last month I heard it again, word for word, from a sales director I was interviewing for a corporate client. Ten years. Same process. Delivered with full confidence.
> In June my mentorship joined a client who is not your typical agent.  
> He co-owns a real estate company and runs his own social media marketing agency. His job is to generate leads for the same business he co-owns. 
> So when the leads do not convert, he is losing money twice.
> He came to me because something was not working. I asked him to describe the sales process. He did it in thirty seconds.
> Call the client. Find out what they want. Send the brochures. Follow up. Follow up again. Pray.
> Last was a Joke of course...
> Or the premium version: call the client, pitch the newest launch, invite them to the sales centre, push the expression of interest form.
> 
> I have been talking about this for years. 
> 
> And for a long time, agencies could survive it because there were enough leads and enough lucky closings to keep the numbers looking acceptable.
> 
> That is changing. Leads are more expensive. Clients are more cautious. The volume game is getting harder to play. And people are finally starting to ask whether the process is the problem.
> Most off-plan buyers today are not in Dubai. They are in Europe, the UK, the CIS, Asia. And even those who live here are not jumping in a taxi to a developer sales centre after a two-minute

## Time Management Changes After Six Months

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-08-30 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- After six months, a real estate agent should prioritize money-making activities in their schedule.
  - “This is what changes when your schedule is after your first six months. Your money making activities become the priority.” — [lines 108-108](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000018`)

### Goal

- To ensure that money-making activities are prioritized in the weekly schedule.
  - “money making activities become the priority. Not something you fit, something that you all week is build around.” — [lines 108-108](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000018`)

### Prerequisites

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Steps

1. Dedicate two daily time blocks to dialing prospective clients.
  - “It's two blocks a day, forty-five minutes each. Eight blocks in your week.” — [lines 116-116](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000020`)

2. Place calls before any other task in the calendar.
  - “Two blocks every morning. And they're going into the empty calendar before anything else exists.” — [lines 128-128](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000023`)

3. Group client meetings in the afternoon or evening and focus on content review on Wednesday afternoons.
  - “Wednesday afternoon is the only block in this week that isn't a conversation. It's a content and one hour listening back to your own calls.” — [lines 132-132](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000024`)

## Gratitude Exercise

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** advice · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-07-11T16:08:20Z · **Author:** unknown · **Format:** post

### Summary

- Reflect on how much one would pay to go back to a younger age and consider gratitude for the present life.
  - “How much would I pay to go back to being 26? Or even 36? Honestly? Nothing.” — [lines 14-31](../../data/instagram/posts/2026-07-11-in-20-years-you-would.md) (`instagram-posts-2026-07-11-in-20-years-you-would-md-cd9d349136:u000001`)

### Original context

**authored text by unknown author** · lines 14-31 · authored_text

> ## Caption
> “In 20 years, you would give everything to be where you are right now. At this age, in this body, living this exact life.”
> 
> Jimmy Carr said this on The Diary of a CEO, and the thought genuinely worked. It immediately brought me back to the present.
> 
> But then I reversed the question.
> 
> How much would I pay to go back to being 26? Or even 36?
> 
> Honestly? Nothing.
> 
> I don’t want my old life back. I want this version of it. My people, my health, my body, my business, where I live and everything I have built.
> 
> Maybe in 66… omg that’s a very scary number now… but I want to build every day … to arrive there feeling that’s it’s the best time… not regretting my 40s.
> 
> Would you go back 20 years if you could?
> 
> #Gratitude #PersonalGrowth #LifeReflection #PresentMoment WomenOver40 Midlife

## Strategy to manage instability

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** advice · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-04-14 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- In moments of instability, instead of seeking to feel better first, it's advised to have a simple next step, move, plan, or direction.

You need just a simple next step, a move, a plan, a direction.” — [lines 20-20](../../data/youtube/video/2026-04-14-structure-over-confidence-navigate-life-s-uncertainty-shorts-btMVBcDuMV4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-04-14-structure-over-confidence-navigate-life-s-uncertainty-shorts-cb810d3eb1:u000001`)

### Original context

**olgasi** · lines 20-20 · spoken_turn

> If your life changed overnight, the first thing you need is not confidence, it's a structure. Because when life gets unstable, confidence disappear very fast. And that's when most people start panicking, overthinking, scrolling, freezing, comparing. But in moments like this, you do not need to magically feel better first. You need just a simple next step, a move, a plan, a direction.

## Questions that Harm Sales

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** claim · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-08-13 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Asking clients about their prior visits to Dubai or if they like it does not correlate directly with investment decision-making and may hinder the sales process.
  - “liking Dubai is not an investment decision.” — [lines 70-70](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-13-4-questions-that-kill-your-dubai-real-estate-deals-in-2026-pQCLpcXSx2s.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-13-4-questions-that-kill-your-dubai-real-estate-deals-in-2026-p-56bc27347c:u000009`)
  - “the client freezes because in reality he's not maybe downtown Dubai Marina, maybe one or two more, but he doesn't have enough information to answer you.” — [lines 74-74](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-13-4-questions-that-kill-your-dubai-real-estate-deals-in-2026-pQCLpcXSx2s.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-13-4-questions-that-kill-your-dubai-real-estate-deals-in-2026-p-56bc27347c:u000010`)

### Original context

**olgasi** · lines 70-70 · spoken_turn

> Have you been to Dubai? Do you like Dubai? Many agents believe that if the client has visited or especially more than once and he says it's like it, it's it's already kind of halfway to buying. But liking Dubai is not an investment decision. And then it gets worse. But the client says, yeah, I've been a few times. I I really like Dubai. And the agents get excited. Oh, then you're almost an expert. So which area would you like to invest?

**olgasi** · lines 74-74 · spoken_turn

> Now the client freezes because in reality he's not maybe downtown Dubai Marina, maybe one or two more, but he doesn't have enough information to answer you. So what happens in his mind? I need to see the options first. And what is he telling you? Can you send me some options? Not because he's avoiding you, because your questions forces him to make a decision he doesn't have an information to make. And once again you shut yourself in a foot because if every question you ask

**olgasi** · lines 78-78 · spoken_turn

> pushes the client back to what send me some options, how exactly are you planning to get him to a meeting? And then the most popular qualification question in Dubai real estate. Are you looking for investment or a personal use? I know your manager told you to ask it. And yes, it's important information. But asking in the first minute and the client says investment, what do you actually know now? Nothing. Not what returned he expects, not the like rental

## Questions for Investors

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-06-24 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Before investing, ask yourself six questions to guide your real estate investment decision-making.
  - “Before you buy, ask the six questions. Who is the tenant, buyer, or end user for this property? Why would they choose this location, not somewhere else? What is the demand engine for the next five to ten years? Is it business? Is it metro, airport, family lifestyle, waterfront, the future infrastructure shift? What can push the price up, and what can slow down your exit?” — [lines 218-218](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivSZgOpA.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivs-55e5a76b49:u000045`)

### Goal

- To guide real estate investment decisions.
  - “Do you actually read the buyer map as an investor? Before you buy, ask the six questions.” — [lines 218-218](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivSZgOpA.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivs-55e5a76b49:u000045`)

### Prerequisites

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Steps

1. Determine the tenant, buyer, or end user for the property.
  - “Who is the tenant, buyer, or end user for this property?” — [lines 218-218](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivSZgOpA.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivs-55e5a76b49:u000045`)

2. Analyze why they would choose this particular location over others.
  - “Why would they choose this location, not somewhere else?” — [lines 218-218](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivSZgOpA.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivs-55e5a76b49:u000045`)

3. Identify the demand engine for the next five to ten years \(business, metro, airport, family lifestyle, waterfront, infrastructure shift\).
  - “What is the demand engine for the next five to ten years? Is it business? Is it metro, airport, family lifestyle, waterfront, the future infrastructure shift?” — [lines 218-218](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivSZgOpA.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivs-55e5a76b49:u000045`)

4. Assess factors that can increase property prices and factors that can slow down your exit.
  - “What can push the price up, and what can slow down your exit?” — [lines 218-218](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivSZgOpA.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivs-55e5a76b49:u000045`)

## YouTube Video Editor Role Description

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** offering · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-05-19T05:22:00.355000Z · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** post

### Summary

- Olga Sinenko is seeking a strong long-form YouTube video editor for a remote, part-time role to create 4 long-form YouTube videos per month, each up to 20 minutes long, using Adobe Premiere Pro.
  - “I’m looking for a strong long-form YouTube video editor to join the team.” — [lines 10-34](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel-md-a97f68d121:u000001`)
  - “Remote, part time role.” — [lines 10-34](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel-md-a97f68d121:u000001`)
  - “The role: 4 long-form YouTube videos per month Up to 20 minutes per video Adobe Premiere Pro only” — [lines 10-34](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel-md-a97f68d121:u000001`)

### Prerequisites

- Experience editing long-form YouTube videos is required.
  - “experience editing long-form YouTube videos.” — [lines 10-34 part 2](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel-md-a97f68d121:u000002`)

- Familiarity with Adobe Premiere Pro is required.
  - “Adobe Premiere Pro only” — [lines 10-34](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel-md-a97f68d121:u000001`)

### Steps

1. Review the provided script, technical brief, and references.
  - “You will receive a ready script, technical brief and references” — [lines 10-34](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel-md-a97f68d121:u000001`)

2. Collaborate with the producer based on the given brief, direction, and feedback.
  - “You will work closely with our producer, who will provide the brief, direction and feedback.” — [lines 10-34](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel-md-a97f68d121:u000001`)

3. Think creatively regarding the project rather than following instructions mechanically.
  - “I don’t want someone who only follows instructions mechanically. I’m looking for someone who can think with the project.” — [lines 10-34](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel-md-a97f68d121:u000001`)

### Constraints

- The role requires editing capability specifically in long-form videos; experience with Shorts, Reels, or TikToks is insufficient.
  - “Experience with Shorts, Reels or TikToks is not enough for this role.” — [lines 10-34](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel-md-a97f68d121:u000001`)

- Adobe Premiere Pro only.
  - “Adobe Premiere Pro only” — [lines 10-34](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-19-im-growing-my-youtube-channel-md-a97f68d121:u000001`)

### Original context

**authored text by olgasi** · lines 10-34 · authored_text

> I’m growing my YouTube channel, @OlgaSinenkoRealEstate, and I’m looking for a strong long-form YouTube video editor to join the team.
> Remote, part time role.
> 
> Most video editors can cut.
> Very few can tell a story.
> And this is exactly the difference I’m looking for.
> You will work closely with our producer, who will provide the brief, direction and feedback.
> You will receive a ready script, technical brief and references, but I don’t want someone who only follows instructions mechanically.
> I’m looking for someone who can think with the project.
> 
> The role:
> 4 long-form YouTube videos per month
> Up to 20 minutes per video
> Adobe Premiere Pro only
> 
> Test task required
> Important:
> Experience with Shorts, Reels or TikToks is not enough for this role.
> I’m looking specifically for someone with experience editing long-form YouTube videos.
> 
> The selection process will include:
> Portfolio review
> A short test task: editing a 2-minute intro
> 
> Be first to APPLY - ONLY VIA https://lnkd.in/dAjUWRMT

>

> 
> So I learned sales by speaking to people who did NOT ask me to call them.
> 
> - People who were busy.
> - People who were not interested.

### Original context

**olgasi** · lines 56-56 · spoken_turn

> I saw a similar shift in 2015 and usually the stage of uncertainty lasts from four to six months. This is the period where sellers are not ready to accept the new reality yet and buyers are already waiting for a discount. But here's what many people forget. During the previous correction, the market did not drop by thirty percent in the first year. It took around four years for the prices to reach minus forty percent.

## Mind's Protective Role

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** claim · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-09-08T06:00:10.742000Z · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** post

> How do you change your income, your life and yourself?
> 
> By the way !!! This is Exactly the main promise behind Tony Robbins and events.
> 
> After four days at Unleash the Power Within in Germany, I would describe his technology in one simple sentence:
> 
> You do not experience life.
> 
> You experience the life you focus on.
> 
> Here is what this actually means.
> 
> A client not answering your call is simply a fact.
> 
> “They have ghosted me. They will never buy” is not a fact.
> 
> It is the meaning your mind gives to the situation.
> 
> And because this explanation comes from your own mind, you immediately believe it.
> 
> But your mind can deceive you.
> 
> Its primary job is not to make you happy, successful or confident. Its primary job is to protect you and help you survive.
> 
> It is constantly looking for potential threats.
> 
> Thousands of years ago, that threat could have been a wild animal.
> 
> Today, it can be a client not answering your call, someone rejecting your offer, a difficult conversation or an uncertain result.
> 
> Your mind sees uncertainty and immediately creates the worst possible explanation to protect you from disappointment or danger.
> 
> Then you react not to what actually happened, but to the story your mind created about it.
> 
> That story changes your emotional state.
> 
> Your emotional state changes your actions.
> 
> And your actions eventually change your results, your income and your life.
> 
> This is why learning to control your focus and emotional state is not just positive thinking.
> 
> It is a practical life skill.
> 
> Change the meaning, and you change your emotional state.
> 
> Change your emotional

  - “This is where neuroemotional persuasion comes in. You learn how to ask better questions. So instead of convincing the client, the client starts convincing himself.” — [lines 38-38](../../data/instagram/posts/2026-09-15-tired-of---i-need.md) (`instagram-posts-2026-09-15-tired-of-i-need-md-a1b2c2f98a:u000003`)

> You probably don't want to hear another real estate sales tip right now. But if you stay with me, this could change the way your clients listen, reply, and move forward. Most agents try to close by pushing harder. They explain more, they send more options, more payment plans, more follow-ups, and the client still disappears. Because sales doesn't happen on the surface. It doesn't happen with more information. It happens inside the

**unknown speaker** · lines 38-38 · spoken_turn

> client's mind. And inside that mind, there is always a battle between fear, doubt, and trust. This is where neuroemotional persuasion comes in. You learn how to ask better questions. So instead of convincing the client, the client starts convincing himself. You stop pitching, you start leading. And this is when they start ghosting. You start booking meetings and you are closing every month. Follow to learn how to close without pushing over explaining.

## Six-Month Agent Schedule

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-08-30 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Develop a weekly schedule for real estate agents under six months.
  - “If you under six months in, your day should not look like a top producer in your team. Copying his calendar is the fastest way to quit this industry.” — [lines 72-72](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000009`)

### Goal

- To prepare new agents to handle real estate conversations under pressure.
  - “Because right now the only product you're selling is your ability to hold the conversation about real estate under pressure.” — [lines 72-72](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000009`)

### Prerequisites

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Steps

1. Spend half of the week on education, market, and product knowledge.
  - “One zone takes half of your week. Education, market knowledge, and product knowledge.” — [lines 72-72](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000009`)

2. Map important city and developer data.
  - “map of the city where the public transfer is going in the next five years.” — [lines 76-76](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000010`)

3. Create and practice presentations weekly.
  - “Every week you build two presentations.” — [lines 76-76](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000010`)

4. Develop confidence through self-assessment with recording.
  - “write the speaker notes, then you record yourself exactly like this.” — [lines 80-80](../../data/youtube/video/2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-LT8S6d8aeYY.md) (`youtube-video-2026-08-30-time-management-for-real-estate-agents-hour-by-hour-schedule-e4701583b6:u000011`)

Education, market knowledge, and product knowledge. Because right now the only product you're selling is your ability to hold the conversation about real estate under pressure. And that doesn't mean scrolling listings, that means a curriculum. First of all, map of

**olgasi** · lines 76-76 · spoken_turn

> the city where the public transfer is going in the next five years. The top ten developers in the history, their stock, and what happened to the project they already handed over. ## Use of Pattern Interrupt

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-05-26 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Using a pattern interrupt can reactivate leads that have gone silent by avoiding typical follow-up messages.
  - “The trick is this, no one wants to admit that he is completely given up on anything.” — [lines 268-268](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000056`)

### Goal

- To reactivate leads that have gone silent after initial contact.
  - “I've seen my coaching client bring back leads that went silent for months just using this exact line.” — [lines 268-268](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000056`)

### Prerequisites

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Steps

1. Craft a follow-up message that challenges the client to reconsider their decision without sounding desperate.
  - “Hi, name? I know life can get busy. Have you completely given up on the idea of making money with Dubai real estate?” — [lines 264-264](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000055`)

### Constraints

- The message should not show desperation or over-eagerness.
  - “If in the moment that you hit the send, your stomach tightens...you just borrowed an adult sentence.” — [lines 268-268](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000056`)

### Exceptions

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

<a id="record-a5380665d4f9fcd9"></a>
## Identifying Trustworthy Real Estate Agents

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-09-25 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- A method to qualify real estate agents involves asking specific questions about recent transactions, upcoming completions, service charges, and potential cons of the property.
  - “Four questions. Ask them and if the agent hesitates, you already have your answer about whether you should work with this person or no.” — [lines 125-125](../../data/youtube/video/2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-3kBUFkV0O9k.md) (`youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2:u000023`)

### Goal

- To assess whether a real estate agent is knowledgeable and trustworthy.
  - “knowing how to qualify the agent in ten minutes.” — [lines 121-121](../../data/youtube/video/2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-3kBUFkV0O9k.md) (`youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2:u000022`)

### Prerequisites

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Steps

1. Ask the agent to show the last three months of transactions in the building or comparable buildings around the area.
  - “Show me the last three months of transactions in this building. And if it's offline in comparable building around the area.” — [lines 129-129](../../data/youtube/video/2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-3kBUFkV0O9k.md) (`youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2:u000024`)

2. Ask about other buildings completing in the same year to assess tenant and buyer options.
  - “what else completes around me in the same year? Because if three other towers handed over the same year, the same month, your tenant has options and your buyer has options.” — [lines 133-133](../../data/youtube/video/2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-3kBUFkV0O9k.md) (`youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2:u000025`)

3. Inquire about service charges and compare them to buildings in the same area.
  - “what are the service charges here and what are the incomparable buildings in the same area?” — [lines 133-133](../../data/youtube/video/2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-3kBUFkV0O9k.md) (`youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2:u000025`)

4. Ask about the cons of the building and potential issues with the developer or area.
  - “What are the cons of the building? What can go wrong with the developer or with the area?” — [lines 137-137](../../data/youtube/video/2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-3kBUFkV0O9k.md) (`youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2:u000026`)

### Constraints

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Exceptions

- If an agent claims there are no cons, they may not know the product well or chose not to disclose information.
  - “if the agent says there is no cons, everything is great, leave. There is no such a thing.” — [lines 137-137](../../data/youtube/video/2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-3kBUFkV0O9k.md) (`youtube-video-2026-09-25-what-changed-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-falling-resales-ha-f4d1591cf2:u000026`)

### Original context

## Property Buying Strategy

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-05-07 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- To successfully buy 'distressed deals' in Dubai, one should not act like a casual buyer but like a 'distress deal hunter,' focusing on preparation and emotional control.
  - “if you're hoping for thirty or even forty percent discount for a really good property, you cannot behave like a casual buyer. You are a distress deal hunter. Your weapon is preparation, your advantage is emotional control.” — [lines 176-176](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sBEJV5Zho.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sbejv5zho-md-5ae767c007:u000034`)

### Goal

- To obtain a significant discount on good properties by taking advantage of distressed deals in Dubai.
  - “if you're hoping for thirty or even forty percent discount for a really good property, you cannot behave like a casual buyer. You are a distress deal hunter.” — [lines 176-176](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sBEJV5Zho.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sbejv5zho-md-5ae767c007:u000034`)

### Prerequisites

- Understand the real estate market by doing proper research using property tracking systems to compare past sales and rental transactions.
  - “Do your search, use property finder over you to both have an easy system to track and compare past sales and rental transactions.” — [lines 152-152](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sBEJV5Zho.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sbejv5zho-md-5ae767c007:u000028`)

### Steps

1. Shortlist your project based on unit type, square footage, developer, layout, and budget.
  - “based on unit type, square footage, developer, layout, budget. Do your search, use property finder over you to both have an easy system to track and compare past sales and rental transactions.” — [lines 152-152](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sBEJV5Zho.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sbejv5zho-md-5ae767c007:u000028`)

2. Check the building reality and potential issues by reading tenants' and owners' reviews, not just brochures.
  - “Before you fall in love with a discount, check the building reality. You need to understand tenants, complainants, owners, comments, maintenance issue, maybe it has an AC problem, noise, or traffic.” — [lines 156-156](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sBEJV5Zho.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sbejv5zho-md-5ae767c007:u000029`)

3. Avoid using common negotiation methods like WhatsApp offers; instead, use a real check made payable to the owner.
  - “If you want to buy a distress deal, you must act differently. Not with the WhatsApp, but with the real check made payable to the owner.” — [lines 164-164](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sBEJV5Zho.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sbejv5zho-md-5ae767c007:u000031`)

4. Prepare early by shortlisting options, checking building conditions, and understanding the real market value.
  - “the best opportunities will not go to people who start searching at the last moment. They will go to buyers who prepare early, shortlisted the options, checked their buildings, and understood the real market value.” — [lines 168-168](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sBEJV5Zho.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sbejv5zho-md-5ae767c007:u000032`)

5. Negotiate on multiple units simultaneously, stay emotionally detached, and act quickly when a suitable deal arises.
  - “Start negotiating multiple units, stay emotionally detached and move fast when the right deal comes.” — [lines 172-172](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sBEJV5Zho.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-07-why-most-distressed-deals-in-dubai-are-fake-05sbejv5zho-md-5ae767c007:u000033`)

## Dubai agents practices critique

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** belief · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-08-25T04:15:01.448000Z · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** post

### Summary

- Most Dubai agents are not scamming anyone, but are using bad advice and doing what they were taught.
  - “most of Dubai agents weren't scamming anyone - IM HERE TO WITNESS. You are Good people -” — [lines 10-56](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-08-25-dubai-agents-are-scammers-a.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-08-25-dubai-agents-are-scammers-a-md-347b6da663:u000001`)

### Original context

**authored text by olgasi** · lines 10-56 · authored_text

> "Dubai agents are scammers..."
> 
> A client said that to me this week.
> 
> I coach agents. But clients pay for my Coaching too - buyers and tenants who want someone to walk the market with them. 
> 
> Why do they pay? 
> 
> Because honesty failed everywhere else. 
> 
> A man is paying out of his own pocket for what an agent should give him for free.
> 
> His story. Unit advertised at 120. He messages the agent - The response form agent -' First come, first serve. and its 130 for one or two cheques. and135 for two to four.'
> One number in the ad, three in the chat. 
> 
> Guess what the client did?
> Closed the conversation!
> Ok - He's renting. 
> Bur your 4M off-plan buyer thinks exactly the same way. 
> 
> Here's the uncomfortable part: most of Dubai agents weren't scamming anyone - IM HERE TO WITNESS.
> 
> You are Good people - just using bad ADVICE and doing what you were taught.
> 
> In my career I've seen around 50 tactics while selling myself, then coaching agents to sell. 
> Some work. 
> Some work sometimes. 
> Most are old abd whatever your favourite top closer does on stage was never built for your client.
> You think you're using a technique. 
> The clients reads it - SCAMM. He doesn't argue - he just stops replying.
> 
> Top 5 to avoid in 2026:
> 1. Opening with pressure. First come, first serve. Last unit. Last price. You haven't asked him anything and you're already squeezing.
> 
> 2. Asking nothing but budget. He gives you a number, you tell him it's too low and he needs to pay more. You learned one thing about him and used it against him - he will never opens up.
> 
> 3. Pushing an offer below what you just said the owner

## Top 5 tactics for agents to avoid

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** advice · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-08-25T04:15:01.448000Z · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** post

### Summary

- Agents should avoid using pressure tactics such as 'first come, first serve', ignoring client needs aside from budget, offering deals below what the owner will accept, focusing solely on money matters, and not knowing detailed information about listings.
  - “Top 5 to avoid in 2026: 1. Opening with pressure. First come, first serve. Last unit. Last price. You haven't asked him anything and you're already squeezing.” — [lines 10-56 part 2](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-08-25-dubai-agents-are-scammers-a.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-08-25-dubai-agents-are-scammers-a-md-347b6da663:u000002`)
  - “3. Pushing an offer below what you just said the owner would take. Usually because you're reviving the deal the previous client walked away from.” — [lines 10-56 part 2](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-08-25-dubai-agents-are-scammers-a.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-08-25-dubai-agents-are-scammers-a-md-347b6da663:u000002`)
  - “4. Ignoring everything except the money. He tells you size, layout, who's living there, what he's already rejected.” — [lines 10-56 part 3](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-08-25-dubai-agents-are-scammers-a.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-08-25-dubai-agents-are-scammers-a-md-347b6da663:u000003`)
  - “5. Not knowing your numbers. Square footage. Price per square foot. His currency.” — [lines 10-56 part 3](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-08-25-dubai-agents-are-scammers-a.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-08-25-dubai-agents-are-scammers-a-md-347b6da663:u000003`)

>

> Some work sometimes.

> You think you're using a technique. 
> The clients reads it - SCAMM. He doesn't argue - he just stops replying.
> 
> Top 5 to avoid in 2026:
> 1. Opening with pressure. First come, first serve. Last unit. Last price. You haven't asked him anything and you're already squeezing.
> 
> 2. Asking nothing but budget. He gives you a number, you tell him it's too low and he needs to pay more. You learned one thing about him and used it against him - he will never opens up.
> 
> 3. Pushing an offer below what you just said the owner would take. Usually because you're reviving the deal the previous client walked away from. People aren't stupid. They know when they're solving someone else's problem.
> 
> 4. Ignoring everything except the money. He tells you size, layout, who's living there, what he's already rejected. You send whatever fits the budget line. With your budget you can only get this. The clients know - you are pushing your STOCK.
> 
> People want to be heard. When your manager said open your ears and close your mouth, that's what he meant.
> 
> 5. Not knowing your numbers. Square footage. Price per square foot. His currency. Go vague and he decides you don't know your own stock. He'll make this decision once or twice in his life. He won't hand it to someone guessing.
> 
> None of this makes you dishonest - but most of the

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-03-30 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Reframing the idea that the market has stopped into a recognition of market shifts and intelligent buying.
  - “when you're talking to an investor and you are selling an off-plan and this is an off-plan investor, you have to reframe the general idea that he will bring to the table.” — [lines 44-44](../../data/youtube/video/2026-03-30-if-client-is-telling-you-i-m-hearing-alot-of-negative-new-ab-l2mO_ptlfk8.md) (`youtube-video-2026-03-30-if-client-is-telling-you-i-m-hearing-alot-of-negative-new-ab-14701f23af:u000004`)

### Goal

- To change the client's perception from believing the market has stopped to recognizing market shifts and intelligent buying.
  - “Yes, Mr. client, I know it may look like the market has stopped. But reality is, the market shifted. Now, people are buying very smart. Demand didn't disappear. Buyers became more selective.” — [lines 60-60](../../data/youtube/video/2026-03-30-if-client-is-telling-you-i-m-hearing-alot-of-negative-new-ab-l2mO_ptlfk8.md) (`youtube-video-2026-03-30-if-client-is-telling-you-i-m-hearing-alot-of-negative-new-ab-14701f23af:u000008`)

- To uncover the candidate's actual level of understanding and competence in sales management.
  - “That is usually when the truth comes out.” — [lines 10-88 part 2](../../data/linkedin/posts/2026-05-27-if-you-have-a-wrong.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-05-27-if-you-have-a-wrong-md-f68cc20701:u000002`)

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

> And how to stop relying on:
> 
>                                                   Hopefully this call went well.
> That is a skill.
> And it can be learned.
> I know because I had to learn it myself.
> 
> And later, I had to learn how to teach it to other people.
> 
> If every new client still feels like a new experiment, despite all the scripts, follow-ups and sales techniques you have tried, the problem may not be what you write after the call.
> It may be that there is no clear system for what should happen before the client gets to that point.

<a id="record-f808c97728698466"></a>
## Three Levels of Confidence

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-07-24 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- There are three levels of confidence in sales: borrowed confidence, knowledge-based confidence, and skill-based confidence.
  - “There are three levels of confidence in sales.” — [lines 114-114](../../data/youtube/video/2026-07-24-the-real-secret-to-success-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-and-ctpRUnC9eg8.md) (`youtube-video-2026-07-24-the-real-secret-to-success-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-and-4c881de4ed:u000009`)

### Goal

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Prerequisites

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Steps

1. Borrowed confidence is when you memorize somebody else's script and you feel confident only when the client follows the conversation exactly as you plan it.
  - “The first is borrowed confidence. This is when when you memorize somebody else's script, objection handler presentation, and you feel confident only when the client follows the conversation exactly as you plan it.” — [lines 106-106](../../data/youtube/video/2026-07-24-the-real-secret-to-success-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-and-ctpRUnC9eg8.md) (`youtube-video-2026-07-24-the-real-secret-to-success-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-and-4c881de4ed:u000007`)

2. Knowledge-based confidence is when you know the project, area, developer, and market, and can explain details and answer questions, but may struggle if the client is emotional, resistant, or uncertain.
  - “The second is knowledge based confidence. This is when you know the project, the area, the developer and the market. You can explain the details and answer the questions. But if the client becomes emotional, resistant or uncertain, knowledge” — [lines 110-110](../../data/youtube/video/2026-07-24-the-real-secret-to-success-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-and-ctpRUnC9eg8.md) (`youtube-video-2026-07-24-the-real-secret-to-success-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-and-4c881de4ed:u000008`)

3. Skill-based confidence is understanding what should happen in the client's mind and knowing what to say to guide the client towards a yes in the sales process.
  - “The third is a skill based confidence. This is when you understand what should happen in the client mind and what you should do and what you should say to engineer between you and the client the yes in the sales process.” — [lines 114-114](../../data/youtube/video/2026-07-24-the-real-secret-to-success-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-and-ctpRUnC9eg8.md) (`youtube-video-2026-07-24-the-real-secret-to-success-in-dubai-real-estate-in-2026-and-4c881de4ed:u000009`)

> ‘Already Living in that Future”... there we had everything we wanted, the money, the attention, the wins.

> And now that future has fallen apart, it feels like everything you worked for was wasted.
> I know that feeling very well...

> 2018 in Dubai - When the market was slowing down, \(many do not know that as they started after 2020\) - where I came up with Rent-to-Own scheme and convinces small private developers in Al Furjan to run it.

**authored text by unknown author** · lines 15-15 · authored_text

> Survival isn't born from panic, but usefulness. Instead of 'What if it falls apart?', ask 'What problem can I solve today that someone will pay for?' Then emotionally. Of course, somebody all can be emotional. For you to survive, you don't have to be the smartest one. You just have to be the most useful one.

<a id="record-1855650ff57286d2"></a>
## Avoid Procrastination

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** advice · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-08-30 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Transactional analysis founded by Eric Bern aids in understanding how communication positions affect interactions. Communicating from a dependent position aligns you in a child role, prompting the client to assume an adult role above you.
  - “Transactional analysis founded by Eric Bern studied how people communicate and how the position you take in a conversation creates the reaction of the other person.” — [lines 164-164](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000030`)
  - “the moment you communicate from dependent position, you start sounding like a child speaking to adult. And your client, he just has no choice but to take the adult position above you.” — [lines 168-168](../../data/youtube/video/2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-MSM6H191dh4.md) (`youtube-video-2026-05-26-the-sales-techniques-nobody-teaches-because-they-actually-wo-b31a69b6e9:u000031`)

<a id="record-ec8ee23e85dc7e0a"></a>
## Growth comparison with other cities

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** belief · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-06-24 · **Author:** olgasi · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Dubai's growth pattern is different from other world capitals, which usually expand from a historical core. Instead, Dubai creates multiple new centers with government planning.
  - “Dubai doesn't work like that.” — [lines 46-46](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivSZgOpA.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-24-the-dubai-areas-that-will-rise-over-the-next-10-years-k4mivs-55e5a76b49:u000002`)

### Original context

**olgasi** · lines 46-46 · spoken_turn

> The difference between the growth of any other world capital and Dubai is not obvious from the beginning. In many countries, the city usually grows from the old center, historical core, and then new districts appear forming a kind of a rings around the original city. In urban planning, this is called moneycentric. In London, Paris, or Singapore, the logic is simple. One center holds business, status, and money. Dubai doesn't work like that.
